rules.name: All-caps label with wide letter spacing
rules.what: Small labels above headings, scroll hints and section heads set in capitals with the letters pushed apart.
rules.why: The single most common decoration in generated landing pages. It signals 'premium' while carrying no information. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element with its own text, not inside nav, where text-transform is uppercase (or the Latin text has no lowercase letters) and computed letter-spacing is at least 0.05em.

rules.fix: Sentence case and default letter spacing. Carry emphasis with weight, size or color.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev
Solo Design, AI design slop tells

rules.name: Em dash or en dash in interface text
rules.what: Long dashes between clauses, or labels shaped like 'WORD, dash, explanation'.
rules.why: A signature of generated prose. In interface labels it reads as template chrome. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Visible text nodes containing U+2014 or U+2013. An en dash between two digits is ignored as a legitimate range. Headings, labels and buttons weigh more than body prose.

rules.fix: Use a comma, a colon, a middle dot, or split the sentence. For ranges use 'to' or a tilde.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Emoji as icons or bullets
rules.what: Emoji and pictographs used for feature icons, headings, bullets and labels.
rules.why: It shows no icon decision was made, and emoji render differently on every platform, which breaks the tone. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Visible text containing Unicode Extended_Pictographic or Dingbats characters. Copyright, registered and trademark signs are ignored, as is text inside user content areas (editable regions, textareas).

rules.fix: Say it in words. If an icon is needed, use one line-icon set throughout.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Tinted pill badge
rules.what: A short label in a fully rounded capsule with a pale colored fill and text in the same hue.
rules.why: Component kits ship it as the default status chip, so generated pages scatter it everywhere, often in four or five hues at once. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: border-radius at least half the height, background a chromatic color with alpha 0.05 to 0.3 or a pale tint (lightness 85% or more), text color within 40 degrees of the background hue, one to three words.

rules.fix: Plain text in the body color, or a neutral outline. If state matters, put it in words next to the value.

rules.name: Colored outline pill badge
rules.what: The same capsule label, now with a transparent fill and a saturated colored border.
rules.why: It is the tinted pill with the fill removed. Swapping one for the other does not remove the habit. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: border-radius at least half the height, transparent background, a border of at least 1px with saturation of 30% or more, one to three words. Buttons and inputs are excluded.

rules.fix: Plain text, or a neutral hairline border with square or slightly rounded corners.

rules.name: Tinted notice band
rules.what: A full-width notice or warning box laid on a pale yellow or blue fill.
rules.why: A template habit that solves information order with a colored surface. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Block at least 80% as wide as its parent, chromatic tinted background, height under 160px, containing an icon (svg, img or icon element) and text.

rules.fix: A neutral surface with a 1px neutral border.

rules.name: Orange 'processing' pill with a glow
rules.what: A progress state shown as an orange pill with a soft glow around it.
rules.why: Decorating the state makes it look like a warning. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: A tinted pill (the AC-04 conditions) with hue 20 to 50 degrees and a colored box-shadow whose blur is 8px or more.

rules.fix: Neutral text with a neutral spinner.

rules.name: Colored status dot
rules.what: A small colored circle placed in front of a label to mean 'live', 'active' or 'online'.
rules.why: A stock dashboard ornament. Color alone carries the meaning, which also fails color-blind readers. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element 4 to 12px square with fully rounded corners, an opaque chromatic background, no text, followed by text. Not flagged when the dot is flat and still and its color is the page's own success or failure token (--success, --danger, --destructive, --error, --delta-up, --delta-down, --positive, --negative on :root). A running animation or a colored box-shadow is always flagged and raises the weight.

rules.fix: Say the state in words. If a mark is needed, use the text color, or the brand's own success or failure token for a real outcome, flat and still.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Monospace font for interface labels
rules.what: Labels, numbers and small headings set in a monospace face outside of code.
rules.why: Borrowed 'developer' flavor. It lowers readability and has nothing to do with the content. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element with its own text outside code, pre, kbd, samp and var whose first available family in the computed stack is monospace. Short texts (labels, captions, numbers) matter most.

rules.fix: Use the text face. For aligned numbers use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

refs.label: Solo Design, AI design slop tells

rules.name: Thick colored accent bar on one edge of a card
rules.what: A card or callout with a heavy colored stripe down its left side.
rules.why: One of the most repeated generated layouts. The bar adds a color without adding order. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: border-left-width (or top) of at least 2px and thicker than every other side, a saturated color (30% or more), and the element has a background or a radius. blockquote gets lower weight.

rules.fix: Remove the stripe. Separate with spacing, a heading, or one neutral hairline.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Glyph inside a filled circle
rules.what: A white check inside a green circle, or an icon on a colored or gray disc.
rules.why: A template part used to dress up check lists and feature lists. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Non-interactive element 16 to 48px square with fully rounded corners and a filled background, whose only child is one svg or a single non-alphanumeric character.

rules.fix: The line icon alone without the disc, or plain neutral text.

rules.name: Heavy contact form in the middle of a landing page
rules.what: A large form with name, company, phone and message fields placed mid page or at the end of a landing page.
rules.why: It fills the ending when there is nothing else to say. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: A form with three or more text inputs plus a textarea on a page whose URL and title do not look like a contact page. Whether the form is really operated cannot be judged from the page.

rules.fix: One button link in the closing section and an email link in the footer.

rules.name: Rainbow charts
rules.what: Every chart series in a different saturated color, bars filled red, yellow and green.
rules.why: When every value gets its own color, nothing reads as important. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Inside an svg of at least 150 by 80px, the shapes whose fill or stroke is saturated (40% or more) cover four or more 30 degree hue buckets. Canvas charts need pixel sampling and are not covered.

rules.fix: Steps of one color, with the brand color only on the series that matters.

rules.name: Flat gray card with a hairline border, everywhere
rules.what: White or gray cards with a 1px gray border and the same radius fill the whole screen.
rules.why: It is the default of popular component kits, so the product looks like an app you have seen before. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Boxes of at least 120 by 60px with an opaque near-white or light gray background (lightness 95% or more), a 1px neutral border on all sides, no box-shadow and radius 6 to 12px. Fires only when four or more exist, because human-made sites use them too. Read together with CMP-04.

rules.fix: Group with surface contrast and spacing, and keep borders only where they are needed.

rules.name: Browser or system default font left as is
rules.what: Headings and body rendered in whatever the browser or the operating system picks.
rules.why: It shows nobody chose a typeface. It also renders differently on every machine. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: The rendered font of h1 to h3 and of body (the first available family in the stack, checked against loaded FontFaces and measured installation) is a browser default serif or sans-serif, or a system-ui alias.

rules.fix: Choose a text face on purpose, load it, and give it a real fallback stack.

rules.name: Ghost button as the main call to action
rules.what: The first and most important button on the page is only an outline with no fill.
rules.why: It looks refined in a mockup and gets lost on the page. The primary action stops reading as primary. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: The first button-like control in the first screen (outside nav) has a transparent background and a visible border.

rules.fix: Fill the primary button. Keep the outline style for the secondary action next to it.

rules.name: Drawn mockup instead of the real thing
rules.what: CSS shapes or a hand-drawn fake screen where a product photo or a real screenshot belongs.
rules.why: It reads like a slide deck, and anyone can tell it is not the product. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: No img, video, canvas, picture, iframe or large background image in the first screen, and an element of at least 240 by 140px that holds six or more text-less decorative boxes nested three levels deep. Illustration-led sites are hard to separate.

rules.fix: A real screenshot or a real photo.

rules.name: Logo or wordmark redrawn, font swapped
rules.what: A supplied logo redrawn as similar shapes, or a wordmark retyped in a system font.
rules.why: When an agent rebuilds an asset from its own understanding, shading and proportions are lost and it shows at once. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Needs the original asset for comparison, so it cannot be measured on an arbitrary site. It is a rule for the generation process.

rules.fix: Use the original pixels or vectors as they are. Export vectors as outlines from the design tool.

rules.name: Generated photo look
rules.what: Golden hour light, glossy skin, bright and saturated generated photos.
rules.why: It is the average of generated imagery, so it reads as AI at a glance. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Needs an image classifier. It cannot be measured from CSS or DOM.

rules.fix: Give real reference photos as input; add film grain, lower saturation, slightly darker exposure.

rules.name: Purple gradient
rules.what: Indigo to violet gradients on hero backgrounds, buttons and headings.
rules.why: The best known generated color choice. It comes from defaults that models have seen thousands of times.

detect.signal: background-image gradient with two or more color stops at hue 230 to 290 degrees and saturation of 40% or more. Weighted by covered area.

rules.fix: Pick one brand color and use it flat. If a gradient is needed, keep it within one hue and low contrast.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev
prg.sh, why AI keeps building the same purple gradient

rules.name: Cream background with a terracotta accent
rules.what: A paper-colored cream or beige page with a rusty orange accent, paired with a large serif.
rules.why: It has become the default look of recent AI tools, a borrowed kind of elegance.

detect.signal: Effective page background lightness 90% or more, hue 30 to 60 degrees, low but non-zero chroma, together with a button or link accent at hue 10 to 30 degrees and saturation 50% or more.

rules.fix: Pure white or a neutral that comes from the brand, and an accent taken from the brand definition.

refs.label: Solo Design, AI design slop tells
Coverage of the Claude design aesthetic

rules.name: Near-black background with a neon glow
rules.what: A near-black page with one neon green or vermilion color made to glow.
rules.why: The default for a 'developer tool' feel. Contrast looks strong but there is no hierarchy.

detect.signal: Effective page background relative luminance of 0.02 or less, plus a saturated (70% or more) accent element with a box-shadow or text-shadow blur of 16px or more.

rules.fix: If a dark theme is needed, separate surfaces with gray steps and keep the accent flat.

refs.label: Solo Design, AI design slop tells
AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Gradient-filled text
rules.what: Headline words filled with a gradient instead of a color.
rules.why: A shortcut to 'exciting'. It lowers contrast and readability, and it ages fast.

detect.signal: Text element with background-clip: text (or the -webkit- form), a gradient background-image and a transparent text fill.

rules.fix: Solid text color. Create emphasis with size, weight or placement.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Green as the replacement for banned purple
rules.what: Once purple is avoided, the same layout returns in emerald or mint green.
rules.why: Only the hue changed; the structure of one accent, a gradient and a glow is the same.

detect.signal: Primary accent at hue 140 to 170 degrees appearing together with COL-01, COL-03 or COL-07 structures. Green alone is normal for many real brands, so it never fires without those structures.

rules.fix: Change the structure (glow, gradient), not the hue.

refs.label: Solo Design, AI design slop tells

rules.name: Rainbow of tinted boxes
rules.what: Every card, badge and icon background gets a different pale tint until the page is a rainbow.
rules.why: Coloring each item looks organized, but color stops meaning anything.

detect.signal: Chromatic tinted surfaces (alpha 0.05 to 0.3, or lightness 90% or more) falling in four or more distinct 30 degree hue buckets.

rules.fix: Neutral surfaces, with color only where it means something (error, success).

refs.label: Solo Design, AI design slop tells
AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Large colored glow shadow
rules.what: Wide, soft shadows tinted with the accent color around buttons and cards.
rules.why: It imitates light that is not there and makes every element compete for attention. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: box-shadow with blur of 24px or more and a shadow color with saturation of 40% or more (not gray or black). Shadows with color alpha under 0.15 are ignored.

rules.fix: No shadow, or a small neutral shadow that only describes elevation.

rules.name: Inter everywhere
rules.what: Every heading and every paragraph set in Inter.
rules.why: Inter is a fine typeface and the default of most starters. Using it for everything is the absence of a type decision.

detect.signal: The rendered font (document.fonts load result plus first available family) of h1 to h3 and of body text is Inter.

rules.fix: Keep Inter for interface text if you like it, and pair it with a face that has a point of view for headings.

refs.label: prg.sh, why AI keeps building the same purple gradient

rules.name: The usual substitute fonts
rules.what: Told to avoid Inter, generated pages move to Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Geist and the like.
rules.why: It is just the second default.

detect.signal: The rendered font of headings or body is in the list (Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Geist, Geist Mono, DM Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans and similar). The list is meant to be updated by measurement.

rules.fix: A face chosen for the brand context, with a one-line reason you can state.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: One italic serif word in the headline
rules.what: One word inside a sans-serif headline switched to an italic serif or a different color.
rules.why: A cliche that imitates editorial taste. It appears in nearly every generated hero.

detect.signal: A child of h1 or h2 that differs from its parent in font family, italic style or color, and whose text is under 40% of the heading length.

rules.fix: One typeface for the heading. If emphasis is needed, rewrite the sentence.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Whole sentence as a giant headline
rules.what: A sentence of more than eight words set at display size.
rules.why: Size fills the space when there is no point to make.

detect.signal: h1 with font-size of 64px or more (measured at the current viewport, best at 1440 wide) and eight or more words (whitespace separated units for Korean).

rules.fix: A short headline, and the explanation at body size underneath.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Extreme negative letter spacing on large type
rules.what: Big headlines squeezed so tight the letters nearly touch.
rules.why: A 'designed' look applied by formula. Past a point it hurts reading, and in Korean it collides syllables.

detect.signal: Element with font-size of 32px or more and computed letter-spacing of -0.04em or tighter.

rules.fix: Use the tracking the typeface was drawn for, or tighten slightly (around -0.01em to -0.02em) and check by eye.

rules.name: The centered hero formula
rules.what: Centered headline, a pill badge above it, two buttons below.
rules.why: Every builder opens with the same sequence, so the first screen reads as a template.

detect.signal: In the first screen, a centered h1 that has a pill-shaped short text element before it and two or more button-like controls after it inside the same container. Thresholds need tuning because it judges composition.

rules.fix: An asymmetric layout that fits the content, with the real product screen or a photo in front.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev
prg.sh, why AI keeps building the same purple gradient

rules.name: Three icon cards in a row
rules.what: Three equal cards, each with an icon, a title and a two-line description.
rules.why: The default frame for features. Whatever the content, the shape is the same, so nothing is read.

detect.signal: Three or more siblings of nearly equal size under one parent, each with an icon, then a heading, then a paragraph in the same order.

rules.fix: A list, a table or a real screenshot, whichever fits the content.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev
prg.sh, why AI keeps building the same purple gradient

rules.name: 01 / 02 / 03 section numbers
rules.what: Small zero-padded numbers stamped above each section or step.
rules.why: Numbering implies a sequence. On most landing pages there is none, so the numbers are decoration.

detect.signal: Two or more small text elements (font-size 24px or less) whose whole text matches ^0[1-9]\.?$.

rules.fix: Remove them unless order truly matters. If it does, number with words in the heading.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: The predictable section order
rules.what: Hero, logo strip, three cards, three pricing tiers, testimonials, footer, in that order.
rules.why: The same skeleton for any product.

detect.signal: Top-level sections are classified (hero, logo strip, feature cards, pricing, testimonial, footer) and their order is compared with the canonical sequence. Four or more in order fires. The result depends on the classifier.

rules.fix: Order the page by what only this product has.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Bento grid
rules.what: Rounded boxes of different sizes fitted together like a puzzle.
rules.why: Learned as 'the current style' and used whatever the amount of information.

detect.signal: A display:grid container with four or more children of at least three distinct sizes, each with radius of 12px or more and a background or border. Real dashboards are hard to separate.

rules.fix: A simple grid sized to the information.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Every gap is the same
rules.what: The space between sections and between cards is one value everywhere.
rules.why: Without rhythm you cannot see what belongs together and what is apart.

detect.signal: Across top-level sections and card groups, the vertical paddings and gaps take two or fewer distinct values with a coefficient of variation under 0.1.

rules.fix: Close relations get small gaps, distant ones large.

rules.name: Announcement pill above the headline
rules.what: A rounded 'New: something' chip sitting right above the hero headline.
rules.why: Copied from a handful of startup sites until it became the default hero opener, usually with nothing new to announce.

detect.signal: Just before the first h1 (previous sibling, or a sibling of its parent), a short text element whose radius is at least half its height.

rules.fix: Remove it. If there is real news, say it in a sentence under the headline.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Card inside a card
rules.what: Bordered or shadowed rounded boxes nested inside other bordered or shadowed rounded boxes.
rules.why: Every container gets the same box treatment, so the page becomes frames inside frames with no hierarchy.

detect.signal: An element with a full border or a box-shadow and a radius whose descendant (inputs, buttons and media excluded) meets the same condition and is at least 80 by 48px.

rules.fix: Keep the outer container, and separate the inner items with spacing or hairlines.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Rounded square icon tile
rules.what: A pale colored rounded square above a heading with a same-colored icon inside.
rules.why: The default 'decoration box' for icons. It nearly always comes with three cards in a row.

detect.signal: Square 32 to 64px, radius 6 to 16px, chromatic tinted background, a single svg child, and the next sibling is a heading.

rules.fix: Leave the icon on its own, or remove it.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Same large radius and same soft shadow on everything
rules.what: Every box shares one large radius and one gray shadow.
rules.why: It feels stamped out of one kit.

detect.signal: Among boxes with a background or border, 80% or more share one radius of 12px or more, and the box-shadow string is identical and not none.

rules.fix: A radius scale tied to element size, and shadows only on things that float.

rules.name: Glass panels everywhere
rules.what: Frosted, blurred translucent panels used for ordinary content blocks.
rules.why: Blur behind a panel helps a floating bar or a dialog. On static content it is a costly effect with no job.

detect.signal: Three or more elements with backdrop-filter blur that are not nav, dialogs or fixed and sticky bars.

rules.fix: Opaque surfaces. Keep blur for things that float over moving content.

rules.name: Row of three big stats
rules.what: Three big numbers such as '10K+ users, 99.9% uptime, 3x faster'.
rules.why: Many are invented. The structure can be found; whether the numbers are true cannot.

detect.signal: Three or four siblings each holding a big number (with a +, %, K, M or x suffix) and a short label. The structure is deterministic, whether the numbers are invented is not.

rules.fix: Only real numbers, with their source.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Fake terminal hero
rules.what: A window with red, yellow and green dots holding monospace commands.
rules.why: Added for a 'technical' feel even when the product is not for developers.

detect.signal: Three adjacent round elements near red, yellow and green hues followed by a monospace block in the same container.

rules.fix: The real product screen.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Fake trust signals
rules.what: Testimonials from people who do not exist, logo strips of invented companies.
rules.why: It imitates trust and turns out to be false when checked.

detect.signal: The testimonial and logo structure can be found, but truth needs an outside check (reverse image search, confirming the company exists).

rules.fix: Real customers only. If there are none, remove the section.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Three pricing tiers with the middle one raised
rules.what: Three price cards where only the middle one gets a colored border, a badge or a scale up.
rules.why: The same scene in every SaaS template.

detect.signal: Three sibling cards with a currency amount where only the middle one differs in border color, scale or badge text.

rules.fix: Three tiers only when there really are three; mark the recommendation in words.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: A subscribe form at the end of every page
rules.what: An email field at the bottom of every page, with a thank-you message even though nothing is sent.
rules.why: The ending people add when there is nothing to end with.

detect.signal: One email input with a button just before the footer. Whether it sends anything needs network observation.

rules.fix: Only a newsletter that is actually run.

rules.name: Dark only, no light mode
rules.what: Only a dark screen, ignoring the visitor setting.
rules.why: Dark is used as the default for 'refined'.

detect.signal: The effective page background is dark, no stylesheet rule uses prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme does not include light, and no theme toggle is found.

rules.fix: Define both modes in tokens.

rules.name: Aurora or mesh blob background
rules.what: Large blurred color blobs or radial glows floating behind the hero.
rules.why: Mood without content. It is the background that generated heroes reach for when there is nothing to show.

detect.signal: An element (or its ::before and ::after) with filter: blur of 40px or more, or one that covers 30% of the screen with a radial-gradient background. Only gradients with at least one saturated color stop count; black or white alpha vignettes over photos do not. Blurred blobs count only when the blur is 40px or more on a box of at least 200 by 200.

rules.fix: Show the product, a real photo, or nothing. A flat background is a valid choice.

rules.name: The same few stock icons on repeat
rules.what: A handful of default icons (lightning, shield, sparkles) used over and over.
rules.why: It is the builders' default icon set, so it becomes a fingerprint.

detect.signal: Count and variety of svg elements with a lucide class or a data-lucide attribute. Whether an svg was drawn by AI cannot be judged.

rules.fix: Icons only where they help, chosen within one set for their meaning.

rules.name: Icons from more than one set
rules.what: Icons from two libraries on one page, or outline and filled glyphs mixed in the same interface.
rules.why: Builders pull a glyph from whichever library has it. Two drawing styles side by side show that nobody chose a set.

detect.signal: Small square icons (10 to 40px, inline svg or icon font) outside the identity slot (footer, logos, off-site links, multicolor marks). Flags icons from a second known library (lucide, Font Awesome, Material, Bootstrap Icons, Phosphor, Remix, Tabler, Feather, Ionicons, Iconify), or, with one library, at least two outline and two filled svg icons where the smaller style is 20% or more.

rules.fix: Pick one set and redraw the odd glyphs on its grid and stroke. Filled only as the selected state of an outline icon.

rules.name: Stroke weights that do not match
rules.what: Line icons drawn at clearly different stroke weights on one page, such as 1.5 next to 2.5.
rules.why: Stroke weight is what makes a set read as one family. Mixed weights come from pasting icons from different sources or sizes.

detect.signal: Outline svg icons (10 to 40px) outside the identity slot, stroke width normalized to a 24 unit grid and rounded to 0.25. With four or more icons and at least two weights used twice, flags icons whose weight is 1.4 times or more away from the most common weight.

rules.fix: One stroke width for the whole set, between 1.5 and 2 on a 24 grid.

rules.name: An icon on every card
rules.what: Each card or item in a group of three or more opens with a decorative icon above its heading and description.
rules.why: The icon is there because the slot looked empty, not because it says something. It is the most common way generated pages fill feature sections.

detect.signal: Three or more siblings outside nav, header and footer, each containing a heading and a description of four words or more, where the first visible element is an icon (svg, icon font or image up to 48px) that is decorative (not inside a control, no accessible name, empty alt) and comes before the heading.

rules.fix: Decide the slot first. Feature cards rarely need an icon: remove it, or replace it with a number, a label or a real screenshot.

rules.name: The same entrance animation on every block
rules.what: Every block fades in from below as you scroll, or bounces with an overshooting ease.
rules.why: Motion repeated without meaning makes the page feel slow.

detect.signal: Static signals of a reveal pattern: reveal classes or data-aos attributes, below-the-fold elements waiting at opacity 0 with a translateY, or keyframes that animate opacity plus translate, on half or more of the sections. Overshoot easing (cubic-bezier with values outside 0 to 1) is also reported. Scroll replay would give better accuracy.

rules.fix: Motion only for changes of state.

rules.name: Generated copy voice
rules.what: Weightless parallel lines like 'Build faster, ship smarter' and 'not X, but Y' constructions.
rules.why: A sentence that fits any product says nothing. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: A list of stock phrases can produce candidates, but judging needs meaning. Separate lists per language are required. detect.js reports candidates only.

rules.fix: One concrete fact only this product can claim.

refs.label: AI Slop Detector by Made with Jev

rules.name: Korean words broken mid-word
rules.what: Korean lines that wrap in the middle of a word because word-break was left at the default.
rules.why: Browsers may break between any two Hangul syllables. Lines that split a word read as careless to every Korean reader. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element whose text is at least 50% Hangul, with word-break other than keep-all, where a Range measurement shows a line ending between two Hangul syllables of the same word.

rules.fix: word-break: keep-all on Korean text, with overflow-wrap: anywhere as a safety net for long strings.

rules.name: Only a Latin font declared for Korean text
rules.what: The font stack lists only Latin faces, so Hangul falls back to the operating system font.
rules.why: Mac and Windows render different Korean faces, and Latin and Hangul weights and sizes stop matching. A trace of an English default left as is. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element with Hangul text whose font stack has at least one named family but none of them is a known Korean font or measures as Hangul-capable (checked with loaded FontFaces and a canvas width test).

rules.fix: Declare a Korean face on purpose, in the intended order with the Latin face.

rules.name: Tight line height on Korean text
rules.what: Korean paragraphs set with the line height tuned for Latin text.
rules.why: Hangul is dense and square. A line height that suits English makes Korean paragraphs feel cramped. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Body-like element (not a heading, font-size 28px or less) with at least 50% Hangul and two or more lines whose line-height divided by font-size is under 1.5.

rules.fix: 1.6 to 1.8 for Korean body text.

refs.label: W3C Requirements for Hangul Text Layout

rules.name: Uppercase transform on Korean text
rules.what: text-transform: uppercase applied to labels that contain Korean.
rules.why: Hangul has no capitals, so the style does nothing for Korean and only shows a Latin template was translated without review.

detect.signal: Element with text-transform: uppercase whose text contains Hangul.

rules.fix: Remove the transform. Style Korean labels with weight and size.

rules.name: Letter spacing that is too wide or too tight on Korean
rules.what: Korean text tracked out like an English label, or squeezed like an English headline.
rules.why: Hangul syllables are already evenly spaced. Wide tracking breaks words apart and tight tracking makes syllables collide.

detect.signal: Element containing Hangul with computed letter-spacing above 0.05em or below -0.03em.

rules.fix: Default tracking, or a very small negative value on large headings, checked by eye.

refs.label: W3C Requirements for Hangul Text Layout

rules.name: Fake italic on Korean
rules.what: Italic applied to Hangul, which the browser slants artificially.
rules.why: Korean fonts almost never have italics. Carrying the one-italic-word cliche into Korean gives squashed letters.

detect.signal: font-style italic or oblique on an element with Hangul text, with no loaded italic FontFace for any family in its stack.

rules.fix: Emphasize with weight or color.

rules.name: Translated-sounding generated Korean copy
rules.what: Literal translations of English marketing lines that sound foreign in Korean.
rules.why: Korean readers notice the machine at once. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: A list of stock phrases gives candidates, but judging needs meaning. detect.js reports candidates only.

rules.fix: Short, concrete sentences written as if Korean came first.

rules.name: Missing or wrong lang attribute on a Korean page
rules.what: A page written in Korean that declares lang="en" or no language at all.
rules.why: Line breaking, font fallback and screen readers all depend on it. Generated starters ship lang="en".

detect.signal: Visible body text is at least 50% Hangul but documentElement.lang does not start with ko.

rules.fix: <html lang="ko">, and lang="en" on English passages inside.

rules.name: English button labels on a Korean page
rules.what: The body is Korean but buttons still say 'Get started' or 'Learn more'.
rules.why: A trace of template defaults left unchanged.

detect.signal: On a page that is at least 50% Hangul, button-like controls whose text is Latin only and matches common call-to-action phrases. Brand names in Latin must be told apart.

rules.fix: Korean button labels that name the action.

rules.name: Justified Korean paragraphs
rules.what: Korean body text aligned to both edges.
rules.why: Browsers justify Korean by stretching the gaps between syllables, which leaves uneven rivers of space. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Paragraph with at least 50% Hangul and three or more lines whose text-align is justify.

rules.fix: Left alignment.

rules.name: Korean body text that is too small
rules.what: Korean captions and body copy set below 13px.
rules.why: Hangul strokes fill in at small sizes much sooner than Latin letters do. Seen again and again in our own work.

detect.signal: Element with own Hangul text whose computed font-size is under 13px. Footer and legal text carries lower weight. Only checked on text that is at least half Hangul and at least 10 characters without spaces, so one word navigation labels are skipped.

rules.fix: 14px or more for Korean captions and 16px or more for body text.

rules.name: Page wider than the screen
rules.what: The page scrolls sideways because an element sticks out past the right edge of the viewport.
rules.why: A card name cut to a single letter at a tablet width shipped once with every check green. Layouts tested at one phone width and one desktop width break in between.

detect.signal: documentElement.scrollWidth is more than 1px wider than clientWidth. The finding is the first element whose right edge passes the viewport while its parent does not, skipping fixed and sticky layers and anything inside a scroll or clip container.

rules.fix: Let the element shrink (min-width: 0 on flex and grid children, max-width: 100% on media), wrap long strings, and put wide tables or code in their own scroll box.

rules.name: Text cut off by its box
rules.what: A short label or name cut by overflow or an ellipsis, or a label that spills past the edge of its button.
rules.why: A card name cut to a single letter at a tablet width shipped once with every check green. Layouts tested at one phone width and one desktop width break in between.

detect.signal: Element with its own text, overflow-x hidden or clip or text-overflow ellipsis, and scrollWidth more than 1px past clientWidth: reported when the text is 24 characters or fewer or fewer than about 3 characters stay visible. Buttons, inputs and labels whose text rectangle passes their own edge are reported as spill.

rules.fix: Give the label room (wrap it, let the box grow, or move secondary text below). Truncate only long titles, keep at least the first words visible, and show the full text on hover or focus.

rules.name: Letters stacked one per line
rules.what: A column so narrow that a word wraps letter by letter down the screen.
rules.why: A card name cut to a single letter at a tablet width shipped once with every check green. Layouts tested at one phone width and one desktop width break in between.

detect.signal: A text node with 3 or more characters that renders on 3 or more lines with at most 1.5 characters per line, measured with Range.getClientRects.

rules.fix: Set a minimum width on the column, drop to one column earlier, or move the label above the value instead of beside it.

rules.name: Text overlapping text
rules.what: Two pieces of text drawn on top of each other.
rules.why: A card name cut to a single letter at a tablet width shipped once with every check green. Layouts tested at one phone width and one desktop width break in between.

detect.signal: Line fragments of text from different elements that intersect by more than 2px on both axes, after clipping by overflow ancestors. Text in fixed or sticky layers (headers, banners) and hidden or faded text is skipped. Layered hero art can still trigger it on purpose, so treat findings as candidates to look at.

rules.fix: Take the element out of absolute positioning or give it its own row at narrow widths; check line-height and negative margins.

rules.name: Part of the page scrolls sideways
rules.what: A box inside the page hides content behind a sideways scroll at this width.
rules.why: Readers rarely notice a sideways scroll inside a page, so whatever sits past the edge goes unseen. Chip rows and wide tables are fine when they are a choice.

detect.signal: Element other than html and body with overflow-x auto or scroll whose scrollWidth passes clientWidth. Code blocks are skipped. Mark an intended scroll row with data-taster-allow="scroll". Reported as candidates.

rules.fix: Wrap the content, switch a wide table to stacked rows at narrow widths, or mark an intended scroll row with data-taster-allow="scroll" and show that more content follows.

rules.name: Touch target under 44px
rules.what: On a phone or tablet width, a button, field or control under 44px high (an icon-only one under 44 by 44px), or a plain text link under 24px high.
rules.why: The most frequent failure in our own responsive audits by a wide margin. Controls sized for a mouse are missed by thumbs, and a smaller control on a hand held tablet fails the same way.

detect.signal: Runs at viewport widths of 1024px and below. Buttons, inputs, selects, summary, ARIA controls and links styled as buttons under 44px high, or under 44px wide when they have no text. A plain text link is held to the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum of 24px and passes below it when spaced apart (a 24px circle on its center touches no other target). A checkbox, radio or visually hidden input is measured through its label. A link inside a sentence, a disabled control, and anything hidden or off screen are skipped.

rules.fix: Make controls 44px on touch screens and shrink them only for a wide screen without a coarse pointer, for example @media (min-width: 1024px) and (not (pointer: coarse)). Do not key the small size on pointer: fine, which a headless browser does not report.

rules.name: Text that does not stand out from its background
rules.what: Text whose contrast against the surface behind it is under 4.5:1, or under 3:1 for large text.
rules.why: Low contrast secondary text on a slightly lighter card came back again and again in our own work. A gray that reads on the page background can fail on the card it is placed in.

detect.signal: For each element with its own text, the text color (with alpha and ancestor opacity) is blended over the composited background colors of its ancestors and compared with the WCAG contrast formula. Large text is 24px, or 18.66px at weight 700. Text over an image, video, gradient or a positioned layer that is not its ancestor is skipped, because the color under it cannot be read from styles. Disabled, aria-hidden and faded out text is skipped.

rules.fix: Raise the text token, not each instance: check the smallest text color against the surface closest to it in lightness, for example a muted card, in both themes.

rules.name: Empty value traces on screen
rules.what: Words like undefined, NaN, null, [object Object] or Invalid Date, or two separators with nothing between them, shown to the reader.
rules.why: A missing value printed as code tells the reader the screen is broken. A fake zero is worse because it looks true; leave the value out and say why.

detect.signal: Visible text outside code, pre, kbd and textarea that contains undefined, NaN, [object Object] or Invalid Date as a word, null as the whole text or after a colon, or two middle dots with only space between them.

css.tokens: undefined NaN null [object Object] Invalid Date

rules.fix: Render a missing value as a middle dot or a short sentence ("Not measured yet"), never as the raw value or a fake zero, and drop the separator when a field is empty.
